terms.grammar: noun phrase: minister with the adjective prīmārius
terms.comment: Prīmārius, of the first rank, is classical: prīmārius vir populī (Cic. Sen. 61, Lewis & Short). No Roman office answered to a prime minister: under the Republic the two consuls were the highest magistrates, and under the emperors the emperor governed.

terms.grammar: noun phrase: administer with the adjective prīmārius
terms.comment: Egger’s phrase; Morgan–Owens also gives Egger’s fuller praeses cōnsiliī administrōrum reī pūblicae, president of the council of ministers.

sources: Lewis & Short: minister · Lewis & Short: primarius · Lewis & Short: administer
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. minister: prime minister.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 364.
